language.note: Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where an indigenous language (Guaraní) remains a majority daily language — roughly 70% of the population aged 5+ speaks it daily, not merely as a symbolic minority-recognition language

terrainDescription.zh: 東部為農業與牧草平原，西部查科地區則是乾燥的稀樹草原與灌木林，全國地勢普遍平坦。
terrainDescription.en: The east is agricultural/ranching plains, while the western Chaco region is dry savanna and scrubland; the country overall is quite flat.

plate.color: white background, black text/frame; blue Mercosur band at top (adopted July 2019)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Not strongly documented in available sources — treat as unconfirmed rather than guessed

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not strongly documented specifically for Paraguay — inferred regional similarity to neighboring countries' concrete poles, lower confidence

historicalContext.zh: 巴拉圭是美洲唯一原住民語言（瓜拉尼語）仍為多數人口日常語言的國家——約七成五歲以上人口日常使用瓜拉尼語，並非僅具象徵性的少數承認語言；巴拉圭道路標誌手冊參考美國 MUTCD、墨西哥、中美洲、哥倫比亞與智利等多方標準，屬混合系統。
historicalContext.en: Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where an indigenous language, Guaraní, remains a majority daily language — roughly 70% of the population aged 5+ speaks it daily. Paraguay's road-sign manual draws on the US MUTCD, Mexico, Central America, Colombia, and Chile — a genuine hybrid system rather than a pure Vienna Convention design.
